question: In which of the following styles of temple architecture the shikhara is called deul?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** shikhara is called deul in the Nagara style of temple architecture in Odisha, Indi**a.
 
• In Odisha,** the shikhara is called deul **and is vertical until it suddenly curves inwards at the top. 
 
• The **deul is preceded by a mandap called jagamohana. **
 
• **The exteriors of Nagara style temples are beautifully carved, but the interiors are usually plain. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Northern India saw a rise in the popularity of temple architecture in the Nagara style.
 
• It typically lacks ornate boundary walls or entrances.
 
• The tallest tower is always exactly beneath the garbhagriha.
 
• There is an installation of Amalaka or Kalash on Shikhara.
 
• Nagara temples can be divided into many different types according to the shikhara's shape:
 
 
• Valabhi: Temples built in the Valabhi style are rectangular and have barrel-vaulted roofs.
 
• Wagon vaulted buildings and constructions get their name from having a vaulted chamber roof.
 
• Phamsana: These are shorter, but wider constructions made comprised of roofs with multiple slabs that rise up in a gradual slope on a straight incline like a pyramid meeting at one point over the middle of the building.
 
• Rekha-Prasad: A straightforward Shikara with a square base and inwardly curved walls with a pointed top distinguish Rekha-Prasad or Latina temples.
